brand.tagline: Click the map for every district you're in, and who represents you.

head.title: What district am I in? Find your Wisconsin district — districtry Wisconsin
head.description: Enter an address or ZIP — or tap the map — to find your district: county, city, village or town, school district, Wisconsin Senate and Assembly districts, U.S. House district, and who represents you. Free, no login.
head.og_title: What district am I in? — districtry Wisconsin
head.og_description: Click the map or search any Wisconsin address to see every civic district that covers it, and who represents you.
head.og_image_alt: districtry Wisconsin — a map of Wisconsin with the question: which districts cover this point, and who represents you?
head.twitter_title: What district am I in? — districtry Wisconsin
head.twitter_description: See every civic district that covers a Wisconsin address, and who represents you.

layers.label: Court of Appeals District
layers.rank_note: Four appellate districts — the broadest sub-state boundary the app draws, above the eight congressional districts

source.answers: The Court of Appeals district whose judges hear appeals from the point's circuit court, with all of that district's judges — elected by district — their direct phones, and the district's chambers.

boundary.label: Derived county unions — no agency publishes appellate geometry (measured), so no new line is drawn: each district is a union of whole counties from the shipped TIGERweb county file under a double witness that agrees county for county — Wis. Stat. 752.11(1), unchanged since 1977, and the court system's own appeals page, whose lists the weekly roster run re-asserts
Wisconsin Court System — the appeals-district listing the composition is cross-witnessed against

source.people: wi-court-of-appeals-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from wicourts.gov's contact page — the content blocks, never the judges index's nav menu, which is a stale former-judge list (6 of 16 names wrong when measured). The 4/4/3/5 seat split is gated, so a vacancy is read by a human rather than shipped silently; no judge e-mail exists on the host, so none ships.
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide, all 72 counties across 4 districts.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: Congressional districts — the largest districts a state carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (congressional districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide.

source.answers: The Wisconsin State Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: wi-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI — the Open States current-people export (name, party) merged with the Legislature's own senate index page (Madison office room, phone, fax, e-mail, the current session link; the member's home Voting Address is refused by construction and the build proves it).
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide.

layers.label: Wisconsin State Assembly District
layers.rank_note: 99 State Assembly districts; three nest exactly inside each Senate district

source.answers: The Wisconsin State Assembly district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (state lower chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: wi-assembly-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI — the Open States current-people export (name, party) merged with the Legislature's own assembly index page (Madison office room, phones, fax, e-mail, the current session link; the member's home Voting Address is refused by construction and the build proves it).
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide.

layers.label: Circuit Court
layers.rank_note: 69 circuits — 66 single counties plus three statutory two-county unions, so marginally broader than the county fabric

source.answers: The circuit court whose bench serves the point — Wisconsin's trial court of general jurisdiction — with every judge on that bench, their branch and direct phone where the court system publishes them, and the courthouse.

boundary.label: Derived county unions — no agency publishes circuit geometry (measured), so no new line is drawn: each circuit is a union of whole counties from the shipped TIGERweb county file, composed under a double witness that agrees exactly — Wis. Stat. 753.06 (one circuit per county except Buffalo+Pepin, Florence+Forest, Menominee+Shawano) and the court system's own circuit listing, re-asserted by every weekly roster run
Wisconsin Court System — the circuit listing the composition is cross-witnessed against

source.people: wi-circuit-judges.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from wicourts.gov's judges table (the bench) joined with its contact directory (branch, direct phone, courthouse). Everyone is titled Judge — appointees filling vacancies are indistinguishable from elected judges in any wicourts source, so the card claims neither; no judge e-mail exists anywhere on wicourts, so none ships.
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide, all 72 counties across 69 circuits.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: Counties, pre-built from TIGERweb at bootstrap; the fork's offline anchor layer

source.answers: Which county contains the point, the county clerk who holds its records and — outside Milwaukee — runs its elections, with the clerk's office, hours and contact.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: wi-county-clerks.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Wisconsin Blue Book's county-officers table (a state publication carrying each clerk's party-or-appointed code) CROSS-GATED against wisconsincountyclerks.org, the clerks' own association (office, hours, phone, fax, e-mail) — WEC's own surfaces refuse automated clients, so the two open publishers witness each other; a name they disagree on ships from the association with the party withheld. Milwaukee's card also states that its elections are run by the APPOINTED county Election Commission (Wis. Stat. 7.20), linked and labeled, its members unnamed because its hosts refuse automation. PHASE 4: the card also names the county's OTHER officers — sheriff, district attorney, executive/administrator (the Blue Book's own CE/CA/AC/CM code decides the elected-vs-appointed label), board chair, treasurer, clerk of circuit court, register of deeds, and coroner or medical examiner — from the same Blue Book's officer tables (wi-county-officers.json), shipped DATED (April 2025) because no second publisher for these offices measures open. The chair column's supervisor count is witnessed against the shipped supervisory geometry (71 of 72 agree; Menominee's 7-vs-5 disagreement between two state publications is pinned and the card claims neither), and the Menominee/Shawano rows carry the book's own shared-prosecutorial-unit footnote (Wis. Stat. ch. 978). The BOARD CHAIR — the one officer who is also a supervisor, elected by each board at its April organizational meeting — is additionally reconciled weekly against county-board-members.json: a chair the county's own board page marks supersedes the book's (sourced and said on the card), a book chair absent from a complete county roster is withheld with the reason stated, and the 50 counties publishing no roster keep the dated book row. The county-by-county officer scrape (wi_county_officer_contact_scraper.py) reads nineteen counties' own officer pages weekly — tranche 1's Brown, Burnett, Dane, Eau Claire, Green, Walworth, Washington, Waukesha, Winnebago and Wood, joined in tranche 2 by Dunn, Grant, Jefferson, Marquette, Polk, Portage, Vernon, Washburn and Waushara — adding office phone/e-mail/page links where the page witnesses the shipped name (surname as a whole word plus first-initial nearby; substring matching measured false-positive on 'Community Block Grant' vs Jennifer Grant), superseding the book where a county has visibly moved past it: the first run found Waukesha's own page recording that County Executive Paul Farrow died in office (Interim County Executive Tom Farley ships, and a builder pin refuses the stale name even when the scrape fails) and Walworth's medical examiner turned over; tranche 2's found a SECOND executive the book no longer has right — Portage's own directory and executive-office page both name County Executive Eric Olson where the book has John Pavelski. Milwaukee and Racine county sites refuse this client (403 — the same reason their board rosters ship from GIS layers), and the other measured misses (Bayfield's JS-shell pages, Vilas's officer-less stubs, Dane's unresolvable court/examiner subdomains) are recorded in the scraper's docstring.
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide.

layers.label: 911 Answering Point (PSAP)
layers.rank_note: 95 public safety answering points statewide — most counties are one PSAP, so the average sits just under the county fabric and well above the school tilings

source.answers: The PSAP — public safety answering point — that answers a 911 call placed at the point, per the state's NG911 dataset (the rare overlaps ship exactly as filed). A dispatch-routing fact, never a taxing district or an elected body, so the card names no officeholder. Where a county 911 authority has not filed — three counties, plus provisioning-less Langlade, recorded as gap ng911-psap-filings — the card says so instead of hiding.

boundary.label: Wisconsin Office of Emergency Communications — NG911 PSAPBoundary (statewide aggregate of every county's filing, updated roughly weekly; licence: “This data is free and open for use by the public”), per-agency dissolve pre-built by wi/scripts/build_wi_ng911_service_areas.py on the DsplayName+Agency_ID pair with a 4,000-point name-set agreement gate — the tiling whose FUTURE-dated Expire rows prove the builder's drop-by-date rule

source.people: None, deliberately: an answering point elects no one, and the NG911 schema names centers, never people.
source.applies: Statewide, minus the measured filing absences the Data gaps panel lists.

source.answers: The union high school district serving the point, where elementary and high school districts are separate.

source.people: No roster is joined; the card names the district.
source.applies: Wisconsin — the paired (non-unified) school territory; unified territory answers on the Unified card.

layers.rank_note: Unified (K-12) school districts; pre-built from TIGERweb at bootstrap

source.answers: The unified (K-12) school district serving the point.

layers.rank_note: Elementary (K-8) school districts (TIGERweb School layer 2, live) — the feeder half of the paired territory

source.answers: The elementary school district serving the point, where elementary and high school districts are separate.

layers.rank_note: 579 dissolved EMS dispatch areas statewide — regional ambulance services keep the average above the law layer's 639 and the county-board fabric

source.answers: The emergency medical service dispatched at the point, per the state's NG911 dataset — a response-area fact, never a taxing district or an elected body, so the card names no officeholder. Where a county 911 authority has not filed — four counties plus provisioning-less Langlade, recorded as gap ng911-ems-filings — the card says so instead of hiding.

source.people: None, deliberately: a dispatch service area elects no one, and the NG911 schema names services, never people.
source.applies: Statewide, minus the measured filing absences the Data gaps panel lists.

layers.rank_note: 639 dissolved law-enforcement dispatch areas statewide — sheriffs' unincorporated territory keeps the average above the county-board fabric

A response-area fact, never a taxing district or an elected body, so the card names no officeholder. source.people: None, deliberately: a dispatch service area elects no one, and the NG911 schema names agencies, never people.

layers.label: Fire Service Area
layers.rank_note: 1,046 dissolved fire-department response areas statewide — denser than the law layer (town departments), broader than the county-board fabric

source.answers: The fire department dispatched at the point, per the state's NG911 dataset — the guidebook's operational shape (who responds here), never a fire protection district and never an elected body, so the card names no officeholder. Where a county 911 authority has not filed — five counties, recorded as gap ng911-fire-filings — the card says so instead of hiding.

boundary.label: Wisconsin Office of Emergency Communications — NG911 FireBoundary (statewide aggregate of every county's filing, updated roughly weekly; licence: “This data is free and open for use by the public”), per-agency dissolve pre-built by wi/scripts/build_wi_ng911_service_areas.py on the DsplayName+Agency_ID pair with a 4,000-point name-set agreement gate

source.people: None, deliberately: a dispatch service area elects no one, and the NG911 schema names agencies, never people.

layers.label: County Board District
layers.rank_note: County board supervisory districts — 1,590 across all 72 counties; smaller than a school district, larger than the average town

source.answers: The county board supervisory district covering the point, how many districts that county's board has, and a link to the board itself.

boundary.label: Wisconsin Legislative Technology Services Bureau — WI County Supervisory Districts (Current): the statewide aggregate of every county's twice-yearly filing under Wis. Stat. 5.15(4)(br)1, pre-built and shipped with the app

Trempealeau County — the county's own adopted 2021-2031 plan, shipped in place of LTSB's file for that county alone, which merges its districts 15 and 17 into one and so drops a district the county still elects

source.people: For 22 of the 72 counties, the supervisor holding the district — 20 from each county's own board page and two (Milwaukee, Racine) read as attributes off the county's own GIS layer, Milwaukee's witnessed on every run against the county's Legistar API (county-board-members.json, refreshed weekly by CI as a reviewed PR); a seat the county marks empty renders as vacant. The other 50 counties publish no district-keyed member list this can read, so no name is shown and the card links the county board — Wisconsin has no statewide roster of county supervisors.
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide, all 72 counties.

layers.label: County Subdivision
layers.rank_note: Towns / county subdivisions (TIGERweb CouSub, live)

source.answers: The town or county subdivision containing the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places / county subdivisions, layer 1

source.people: No roster is joined; the card names the subdivision.
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide.

layers.label: Municipality
layers.rank_note: Incorporated places (TIGERweb Places, live); unincorporated points say so

source.answers: The city, village or town containing the point — or that it sits in unincorporated county.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places, layer 4

source.people: No roster is joined yet; municipal officials are a per-county build (docs/EXPANSION_GUIDE.md Part 2.4).
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: Census ZCTAs by Wisconsin envelope (the ZCTA layer has no STATE field); server-generalized

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area containing the point — the Census Bureau's approximation of USPS ZIP delivery areas, not the postal boundaries themselves.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZCTA, layer 11 (ZIP Code Tabulation Areas), live

source.people: No officeholder exists for a ZIP code.
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide.

layers.label: Milwaukee Police District
layers.rank_note: Milwaukee's seven police districts — a seventh of the city each, the largest of the city-scoped tier; the fleet's second city police-district layer

source.answers: The Milwaukee Police Department district covering the point. No captain is named: the city's site refuses automated readers, so district leadership cannot be verified here — the card links MPD's own district pages, which carry it, and the Data gaps panel records the measurement. Outside Milwaukee the layer hides; no statewide who-polices-here boundary publisher exists (that concept's statewide candidate is the NG911 service-boundary route, recorded in the guidebook).

boundary.label: City of Milwaukee — MPD districts, the city's own ArcGIS layer (CC-BY), server-reprojected and pre-built by wi/scripts/build_milwaukee_city_layers.py
City of Milwaukee open data — the same districts as a shapefile (CC-BY), the build-time witness: keys and area shares must agree between the two city surfaces before the file ships

source.people: None shipped, deliberately: MPD publishes each district's captain only behind an access control this project does not defeat, and a name that cannot be re-verified weekly does not ship — the card links the district pages instead (gap mpd-district-leadership).
source.applies: City of Milwaukee only — the layer hides everywhere else.

layers.label: MPS School Board District
layers.rank_note: Milwaukee's eight school board districts — an eighth of the city each, larger than the average aldermanic district statewide; the fleet's second elected school board and this instance's first city-scoped layer

source.answers: The Milwaukee Public Schools board district covering the point, its elected director, and the at-large director the whole city elects — with each seat's term expiration and the Board office's contact. Statute names Wisconsin's districted school boards exactly (most elect at large): MPS and Racine Unified, whose geometry no publisher ships as data — the Data gaps panel records it.

boundary.label: City of Milwaukee — MPS Board Districts, the city's own ArcGIS layer, reprojected by the city's own server and pre-built by wi/scripts/build_mps_school_board_districts.py; the districts were adopted 25 February 2022 (the district's directors page states it) and redraw each census
City of Milwaukee open data — the same districts as a shapefile (CC-BY), the build-time witness: every district's share of the city must agree between the two before the file ships

source.people: mps-school-board-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the district's own directors page (one heading per seat: the at-large president and districts 1-8), cross-witnessed against the board index's committee lists — two surfaces the district maintains separately must name the same directors. The Board's shared contact form and office phone ride the card; outside Milwaukee the layer hides entirely.
source.applies: City of Milwaukee only — the layer hides everywhere else (the MPS tiling is the coverage test).

layers.label: Milwaukee Police Squad Area
layers.rank_note: The 25 MPD patrol squad areas — a twenty-fifth of the city each, nested inside the seven police districts (subOf), between the MPS board's eighths and the aldermanic fabric

source.answers: The Milwaukee Police Department squad area — the patrol/beat subdivision — covering the point, with its parent district. A squad's NUMBER encodes its district (the hundreds digit), and the builder verifies that against the shipped district layer rather than asserting it. No officeholder: a patrol area elects no one. Outside Milwaukee the layer hides, and its toggle nests under the district layer exactly as the reference instance's police beats do.

boundary.label: City of Milwaukee — MPD squad areas, the city's own ArcGIS layer (CC-BY), server-reprojected and pre-built by wi/scripts/build_milwaukee_city_layers.py; each squad is sample-verified inside its hundreds-digit district against the shipped district file
City of Milwaukee open data — the same squad areas as a shapefile (CC-BY), the build-time witness: keys and area shares must agree between the two city surfaces before the file ships

source.people: None, deliberately: a patrol area elects no one and MPD publishes no per-squad roster this project can verify.
source.applies: City of Milwaukee only — the layer hides everywhere else, and its toggle shows only while the Police District layer is on.

layers.label: Aldermanic District
layers.rank_note: 838 city and village council districts — each a union of wards, smaller than a ZCTA, above the ward layer they dissolve from

source.answers: The aldermanic district (in the nine villages that elect trustees by district, the trustee district) covering the point, in the 155 cities and villages whose ward filings compose their districts completely — and, in Milwaukee, Madison, Green Bay, Kenosha, Racine and Waukesha, the alderperson holding the seat.

boundary.label: Derived ward unions — no publisher ships a statewide aldermanic layer, so no new line is drawn: LTSB's statewide ward layer carries each ward's district id (ALDERID), and wi/scripts/build_wi_aldermanic_districts.py dissolves the coded city/village wards on the statewide municipality key. Cross-witnessed against the state's own BAS pre-dissolve, a different filing edition agreeing on all 867 district keys; ten municipalities whose submissions are measurably incomplete (Appleton the flagship) are excluded on the record rather than drawn as fragments
LTSB BAS Live Collection — Alderpersons: the state's own pre-dissolved working set, the composition witness (never the source: no stated terms, mutates mid-collection)

source.people: wi-alderpersons.json, rebuilt weekly by CI for the six big cities with a verified route — Milwaukee's own GIS witnessed against the city's Legistar API, Madison's per-district council pages (the vacant seat named as vacant), Green Bay's staff directory, Kenosha's GIS witnessed against the county's certified April 2026 canvass (which caught and corrected one stale seat), and the Racine and Waukesha council pages. The other 149 municipalities' councils are a recorded gap, never a guess.
source.applies: Wisconsin — the 155 cities and villages that elect council members by district and file complete ward coding; everywhere else the card honestly reports no district.

layers.label: Municipal Ward
layers.rank_note: 7,161 municipal wards — the ballot sub-unit every district is built from; smaller than a ZCTA on average, above the amenity points

source.answers: The municipal ward containing the point — the unit Wisconsin elections are administered by and every supervisory and aldermanic district is composed from — plus which county board district and, in cities that elect alders by district, which aldermanic district it belongs to.

boundary.label: Wisconsin Legislative Technology Services Bureau — WI Municipal Wards (Current): the statewide aggregate of every county's twice-yearly ward filing under Wis. Stat. 5.15(4)(br), queried live (the point query fetches one ward; the map overlay pages the statewide set server-generalized)

source.people: A ward elects no officeholder of its own — it is the unit election administration assigns. No polling place is shown: Wisconsin aggregates polling places only behind a state lookup that refuses automated clients, so the card links that lookup rather than shipping data this project cannot verify (the Data gaps panel records the measurement).
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide.

layers.label: Milwaukee Neighborhood
layers.rank_note: The city's 190 named neighborhoods — an identity fabric, not an electing body; below the ward layer's statewide average, above the amenity points

source.answers: The named Milwaukee neighborhood containing the point — the city's own neighborhood fabric, an identity answer with no officeholder because a neighborhood elects no one. Outside Milwaukee the layer hides; no statewide neighborhood publisher exists.

boundary.label: City of Milwaukee — Neighborhoods, the city's own ArcGIS layer (CC-BY), server-reprojected and pre-built by wi/scripts/build_milwaukee_city_layers.py; names ship title-cased from the city's all-caps values with the raw value kept on the feature, and the build-time shapefile witness caught the city's own two copies spelling one neighborhood apart
City of Milwaukee open data — the same neighborhoods as a shapefile (CC-BY), the build-time witness

source.people: A neighborhood elects no one — the card names the place and stops there.
source.applies: City of Milwaukee only — the layer hides everywhere else.

layers.label: Tax Incremental District (TID)
layers.rank_note: 79 active tax incremental districts — small finance-overlay slices, below the neighborhood fabric's average and above the amenity points; the one city layer that does not tile the city

source.answers: The active Tax Incremental District (Wis. Stat. 66.1105) containing the point, with its number and creation year — a municipal finance overlay that elects no one, the reference instance's tif-district concept under Wisconsin's own name. Most of Milwaukee is in no TID, and the card's standard empty state says exactly that; outside Milwaukee the layer hides.

boundary.label: City of Milwaukee — Tax Incremental Districts, the city's own ArcGIS layer (CC-BY), server-reprojected and pre-built by wi/scripts/build_milwaukee_city_layers.py; the live layer serves only ACTIVE districts, and the builder drops any that gain a past dissolve date

City of Milwaukee open data — the same districts as a shapefile (CC-BY), the build-time witness scoped to the city's own STATUS flag, because the shapefile keeps all 56 retired TIDs the live layer omits

source.people: None, deliberately: a TID elects no one — it is a finance overlay adopted by the Common Council, whose members the aldermanic layer already names.
source.applies: City of Milwaukee only — the layer hides everywhere else, and inside the city most points are honestly in no TID.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: Nearest-3 point layer (807 stations in the state envelope) — not a containment boundary; ranked with the amenity points

source.answers: The three nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a proximity fact, never a jurisdictional claim about which agency serves the point.

boundary.label: USGS National Map — structures, layer 53 (Law Enforcement), live by state envelope; public domain. The envelope deliberately reaches past the state line, so a reader near the border sees the genuinely nearest stations

source.people: Not an elected office — no officeholder is named. The dataset is the same national source the fleet's reference instance ships, ghost records and all: a station USGS has not yet retired can appear, which is why the card presents nearest stations rather than 'your' station.
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide (plus border-state stations the envelope catches, which is correct behaviour near the state line).

layers.label: Fire Station
layers.rank_note: Nearest-3 point layer (1,743 stations in the state envelope) — denser than the police set, so ranked after it

source.answers: The three nearest fire stations by straight-line distance — a proximity fact, never a claim about which department responds to the point.

boundary.label: USGS National Map — structures, layer 51 (Fire Stations / EMS Stations), live by state envelope; public domain. Same envelope-past-the-border behaviour as the police layer

source.people: Not an elected office — no officeholder is named. One ghost record is on the measured record (a department defunct since 2020 still listed), which is why the card presents nearest stations rather than a service claim; the statewide who-responds-here boundary is a separately recorded concept.
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide (plus border-state stations the envelope catches).

layers.label: School Location, incl. private
layers.rank_note: Nearest-3 point layer (2,966 public + private school sites, pre-built) — not a containment boundary; ranked with the amenity points

source.answers: The three schools nearest the point — public and private, each labeled with its kind and grade range — by straight-line distance. A proximity fact, never an enrollment claim: which school a child attends is the district's call (and the state's open-enrollment law reaches across districts), and no statewide attendance-zone publisher exists.

boundary.label: Wisconsin DPI — Public Schools layer (2,138 placed sites of 2,290 records; the 152 records DPI publishes with no location and no address are statewide virtual programs and don't ship on a proximity card), pre-built by wi/scripts/build_wi_school_sites.py
Wisconsin DPI — Private Schools layer (828 sites), same builder

source.people: Not an elected office — no officeholder is named. DPI's own licence terms ride with the data and are why the card claims proximity only: "intended for your reference use only … no guarantee of accuracy is made … not to be used for any land transactions, financial decisions, taxation, surveying, or other similar uses."
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide.

layers.label: Library
layers.rank_note: Nearest-3 point layer (482 public library outlets, pre-built) — not a containment boundary; ranked with the amenity points

source.answers: The three public library locations nearest the point — main libraries and branches both — by straight-line distance, with each outlet's address and phone. Statewide, where the fleet's reference instance answers this for one city only.

boundary.label: Wisconsin DPI — Public Libraries and Branches layer (482 outlets from the annual public library system data), pre-built by wi/scripts/build_wi_libraries.py

source.people: Not an elected office — Wisconsin library boards are appointed (Wis. Stat. 43.54), which is why this concept ships as library locations rather than as a library-district card. DPI's reference-use licence rides with the data, as on the school layer.
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide.

layers.label: Post Office
layers.rank_note: Nearest-3 point layer, straight-line distance — ranked last; not a containment boundary

source.answers: The three post offices nearest the point, by straight-line distance.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures, layer 38 (post offices), live

source.people: Not an elected office; the card lists the facilities.
source.applies: Wisconsin — statewide.

Every county in the state, pre-built from TIGERweb by bootstrap_state.py (bounds tightened to the real count at bootstrap).
The state's U.S. House districts, pre-built from TIGERweb by bootstrap_state.py (bounds tightened at bootstrap).
The state's unified school districts, pre-built from TIGERweb by bootstrap_state.py (bounds tightened at bootstrap).
The 33 State Senate districts plus TIGERweb's ZZ water pseudo-district, pre-built by wi/scripts/build_legislative_boundaries.py (2,000-point agreement gate).
The 99 State Assembly districts plus TIGERweb's ZZ water pseudo-district, pre-built by wi/scripts/build_legislative_boundaries.py (2,000-point agreement gate).

Every county board supervisory district in the state — 1,573 from LTSB's statewide aggregate plus Trempealeau's own 17, built by wi/scripts/build_wi_supervisory_districts.py (numbering, ward-reconciliation and 10,000-in-state-point agreement gates).

The 69 circuit courts as county unions — 66 single counties plus the three statutory two-county circuits (Wis. Stat. 753.06), dissolved from the shipped county file by wi/scripts/build_wi_circuit_courts.py under its partition, merge and containment gates. Rebuild only if the county file or the statute moves.

The four Court of Appeals districts as county unions (Wis. Stat. 752.11 + the court system's own lists agreeing county for county), dissolved by wi/scripts/build_wi_court_of_appeals.py under one-ring contiguity and 72-county containment gates.

The Wisconsin state outline — the coverage wash's REGION band, marking where the statewide layers and the county board DISTRICTS still answer even though no supervisor is named. Split out from metro-outline.json when that became the 20-county roster ring.

Every placed school site in the state, public and private (2,966 at build: 2,138 + 828), pre-built from the DPI org's two school layers by wi/scripts/build_wi_school_sites.py — its gates page past the 2,000-record cap, skip only DPI's placeless virtual-program rows, and witness every point against the layer's own coordinate attributes. Amenity points, not officeholder data: cache-first is fine, and the range tolerates DPI's school-year rotation (WATCH.md).

Milwaukee's seven police districts, the city's own CC-BY layer server-reprojected and witnessed against the CKAN shapefile's area shares (wi/scripts/build_milwaukee_city_layers.py). An operator rebuild; the monthly source report watches both endpoints.

The city's 190 named neighborhoods, same builder and witness — which caught the city's two copies spelling one neighborhood apart (the service spelling ships, the divergence prints every build). Names title-cased for display with the raw all-caps value kept on the feature.

Milwaukee's eight MPS board districts, the city's own layer server-reprojected and witnessed at build time against the CKAN shapefile's area shares (wi/scripts/build_mps_school_board_districts.py). Redraws each decennial census (adopted 2022-02-25); an operator rebuild.

Every aldermanic (and village trustee) district the ward fabric composes completely — coded city/village wards dissolved on the statewide municipality key by wi/scripts/build_wi_aldermanic_districts.py under its completeness, BAS-witness and point-agreement gates (838 districts, 155 municipalities; ten incomplete submissions excluded on the record). Rebuild after each Jan/Jul filing window; a count change is expected news.

Every public library outlet in the state (482 at build), pre-built from the DPI org's libraries layer by wi/scripts/build_wi_libraries.py — whose bbox gate is what catches that layer's measured trap (its LAT/LONG attributes are Web Mercator meters; only the outSR=4326 geometry is real). Same cache posture and annual rotation as the school file.

1,046 fire-department dispatch areas — the OEC's 3,009 effective NG911 FireBoundary polygons dissolved per agency by wi/scripts/build_wi_ng911_service_areas.py (expired rows dropped by date; filing-absence and 100.000% name-set agreement gates). An operator rebuild; the monthly source report watches the layer counts.

639 law-enforcement dispatch areas — the OEC's 3,083 effective NG911 LawEnforcementBoundary polygons dissolved per agency; plain -dissolve, never -dissolve2, so the concurrent-jurisdiction overlaps the counties filed survive (measured). Same builder and gates as the fire file.

95 public safety answering points — the OEC's 205 effective NG911 PSAPBoundary polygons dissolved per agency (11 future-dated Expire rows KEPT, the case that proves the drop-by-date rule; 3 expired dropped). Same builder and gates as the fire/law files; an operator rebuild watched by the monthly source report.

579 EMS dispatch areas — the OEC's 2,443 effective NG911 EmergencyMedicalServicesBoundary polygons dissolved per agency (34 expired rows dropped by date). Same builder and gates as the other three NG911 files; an operator rebuild watched by the monthly source report.

Milwaukee's 25 MPD squad areas — the city's own CC-BY layer server-reprojected, witnessed against the CKAN shapefile's area shares AND sample-verified inside their hundreds-digit districts (wi/scripts/build_milwaukee_city_layers.py). An operator rebuild; the monthly source report watches both endpoints.

Milwaukee's 79 active Tax Incremental Districts — the city's own CC-BY layer server-reprojected, dissolved TIDs dropped by date, witnessed against the CKAN shapefile's area shares scoped to the city's own STATUS flag (wi/scripts/build_milwaukee_city_layers.py). An operator rebuild; the monthly source report watches both endpoints.

rosters.note: U.S. House roster for the state, built from unitedstates/congress-legislators by bootstrap_state.py and refreshed weekly by update-wi-congress-roster.yml (min tightened at bootstrap).
State Senate roster from the Open States current-people export (wi.csv), refreshed weekly by update-wi-legislature-roster.yml; the floor tolerates transient vacancies (33 seats).
State Assembly roster from the Open States current-people export (wi.csv), refreshed weekly by update-wi-legislature-roster.yml; the floor tolerates transient vacancies (99 seats).
The Data gaps panel's content; seeded minimal by bootstrap_state.py, grown as the fork records real gaps.

One row per county: board size read back from the shipped geometry, plus the county's own official page for the card's footer link. Built by wi/scripts/build_wi_county_board_directory.py; not a roster of people — Wisconsin publishes none statewide.

County board supervisors for the 22 counties that publish a district-keyed member list a client can read (476 seats) — 20 scraped from board pages, Milwaukee and Racine read off their own GIS layers (Milwaukee Legistar-witnessed). Built by wi/scripts/build_wi_county_board_roster.py, checked seat-for-seat against the shipped district geometry; refreshed weekly by update-wi-county-board-roster.yml. The other 50 counties name nobody — their cards link the county board instead.

The circuit-court bench — every circuit's judges with branch and direct phone where wicourts publishes them, plus the courthouse — keyed by the same circuit keys the geometry carries. Built by wi/scripts/build_wi_circuit_court_roster.py from the wicourts scrape; refreshed weekly by update-wi-circuit-court-roster.yml, whose composition assertion doubles as the circuit map's redistricting tripwire.

The Court of Appeals bench — sixteen judges keyed by district with role, direct phone and chambers, the 4/4/3/5 seat split gated at scrape time. Built by wi/scripts/build_wi_coa_roster.py; refreshed weekly by update-wi-court-of-appeals-roster.yml, whose composition assertion is the appeals map's redistricting tripwire.

All 72 county clerks — name, party-or-appointed per the Blue Book's own legend, office, hours, phone, fax, e-mail — keyed by county GEOID. Built by wi/scripts/build_wi_county_clerk_roster.py from the two cross-gating open publishers; refreshed weekly by update-wi-county-clerk-roster.yml. Milwaukee's entry carries the statutory election-commission note.

The nine Milwaukee Board of School Directors (at-large president + districts 1-8, keyed to the geometry's DISTRICT values) with roles, term expirations and the Board office's contact, under {members, office, sourceUrl}. Built by wi/scripts/build_mps_school_board_roster.py from the district's own directors page with the committee-list witness; refreshed weekly by update-mps-school-board-roster.yml.

The alderperson roster for the six big cities with a verified, witnessed route (Milwaukee, Madison, Green Bay, Kenosha, Racine, Waukesha — 94 seats), keyed by the municipality's statewide COUSUBFP and zero-padded district id, the geometry file's exact key pair. Built by wi/scripts/build_wi_alderperson_roster.py with per-city, per-field floors and a geometry cross-gate; refreshed weekly by update-wi-alderperson-roster.yml.

72 counties x 7 offices from the Blue Book's county-officer tables (build_wi_county_officer_roster.py; layout-aware x-position parse, chair-seats witness, Menominee pin, shared-DA footnote). Dated April 2025 on every card; refreshed weekly with the clerk scrape.
